note: Checks whose result follows the speed of the machine that runs them. Each was calibrated on the maintainer's machine (Apple M2 Pro), where it passes and where release-cut.mjs enforces it in the staged run of every cut. GitHub's hosted runners are slower and run the three browsers side by side on 3 CPUs, and these checks have failed there on speed alone. With TYPESET_HOSTED_RUNNER=1 (set by ci.yml, nightly.yml and the release workflow's verify job) verify-release.mjs reports a failing check listed here as SLOW, with its detail, and does not fail the run; everywhere else, and with --strict, it is enforced like any other check. An entry needs the runs that show it failing on speed; label is a regular expression over check labels, and browser narrows an entry.

entries.label: ^Typeset(Rich)?Text at 4x CPU: a cold screen push paints every on-screen block composed in its first frame$
entries.reason: The adapters compose on-screen blocks before the first paint unless that work exceeds VISIBLE_BUDGET_MS (120 ms), the engine's safety valve for a very slow device (src/lib/v4/adapter-registry.ts); a hosted runner at 4x CPU is that device.
entries.observed: macos-15 run 36258432379: TypesetText 13 of 16 on-screen blocks uncomposed in the first frame. ubuntu-latest run 36255458992: TypesetText 16 of 19, TypesetRichText 4 of 19. M2 Pro: 0.

entries.label: ^TypesetText in an overflow:auto scroller, scrolled in 0 ms after mounting: no block paints native lines and is rewrapped$
entries.reason: Whether the scroll lands before the visible blocks' first composition finishes is timing.
entries.observed: macos-15 run 36258432379: 1 flash frame (1 block) in 125 frames. M2 Pro: 0.

entries.label: : recomposes after updates with no audit error$
entries.reason: The audit samples each block 260 ms after the fifth update; on a hosted runner the first recomposition can take longer, so the sample catches it in progress (stale-layout, stale-output). Every later sample is clean.

entries.label: ^busy page: visible paragraphs composed within 500 ms$
entries.reason: A wall-clock bound on composing the nine visible paragraphs of a 60-block page; on a hosted runner the same passes take longer.

entries.reason: The adapters compose on-screen blocks before the first paint unless that work exceeds VISIBLE_BUDGET_MS (120 ms), the engine safety valve for a slow device (src/lib/v4/adapter-registry.ts); the hosted runner crosses it, as in the verify-scheduler entry above.

entries.reason: A wall-clock bound on idle-time composition; a hosted runner gets fewer and shorter idle periods.

entries.label: ^education time in the browser: 120 KB of .+ \([\d,]+ characters\) under 100 ms$
entries.reason: One performance.now() sample around a single smartQuotes() call, while the three browsers run side by side on the runner's 3 CPUs, so a pause or a descheduling during that one call counts as education time. The linear-time bound the check guards (the quadratic release candidate took 250 to 776 ms in Chromium) stays enforced on hosted runners by the Node checks on the same code (120 KB under 50 ms) and by the WebKit and Firefox browser checks.
